content: Tengo las imágenes claras. Ahora veo los archivos del servidor para entender los productos actuales antes de hacer todos los cambios.
thinking:
Now I have a clear picture of all three designs. Let me analyze the differences between the current code and what the images show:

**Image 1 - Catalog (vista_de_cliente):**
- Left sidebar: "StoreSync Pro" in blue bold text, below "Admin Portal" text with a storefront icon in a small badge. Nav links: Catalog (active, blue filled), Inventory, Sales POS, Analytics. Bottom: "+ New Sale" blue button, Settings, Support.
- Top bar: Catalog (underlined blue), Inventory, Sales POS links + cart/bell/user icons
- Filter pills: Todo (blue filled), Electrónica, Moda, Hogar, Deportes (all gray)


- Banner section with dark background asking "¿No encuentras lo que buscas?" and a "Sugerir Producto" button in blue
- Product cards displaying full images with category badges in different colors (green for Electrónica, black for Moda, teal for Fotografía, orange for Deportes), AGOTADO overlays where applicable, product names in bold, descriptions, prices highlighted in blue, stock information, and "Añadir al Carrito" buttons

The current code appears fairly aligned with Image 1, though there are some minor spacing and styling adjustments needed. Now looking at **Image 2 - Admin/Inventory (panel_de_administracion):**
- Left sidebar starts with "StoreSync Pro" in bold black and "ADMIN PORTAL" in small gray caps, followed by navigation items (Catalog, Inventory highlighted in blue, Sales POS, Analytics), with Settings, Support, and an admin user avatar at the bottom
- Header displays "Gestión de Inventario" in blue with a search bar, notification bell with a dot indicator, and a cart icon
- Stock summary card shows total items (1,284) and low stock count (12 in a red box) alongside a "+ Nuevo Producto" button
- Storage capacity section includes an icon and progress bar at 82%
- Inventory details table with columns for code, product name, category, price, stock, status, and actions
- Suggestion tray at the bottom listing pending, reviewed, and accepted suggestions from various users

, plus an upcoming orders side panel
- Footer
<truncated 1131 bytes>
s tracks cash received, and a gray "Cambio / Vuelto" box displays the change amount. At the bottom are TICKET and REGISTRAR buttons, with no numeric keypad or quick cash shortcuts visible. The product cards themselves are simplified—just the image dominating the card with name and price below.

I'm also checking the server configuration to see what products are seeded so I can align the POS categories (Bebidas, Snacks, Panadería, Lácteos, Limpieza) with what's shown in the images.

Looking at the different interfaces, the Catalog view needs the sidebar with a two-line "StoreSync Pro" logo in blue and a storefront badge showing "Admin Portal" and "Main Branch", plus the active nav item highlighted. The Admin interface requires user names like "Carlos Mendoza" pulled from the API and a footer with copyright text. The POS interface has the most significant changes—removing the keypad entirely, restructuring the product cards, and updating the category pills to match the specified list.

I need to update the server to include products in those new categories, then rewrite all three HTML files to match their respective designs. Let me start by reviewing what the Catalog currently has versus what Image 1 shows.

The Catalog looks mostly aligned with the category pills and product grid layout, though I might need minor adjustments. The Admin panel has the header and search in place but needs a footer added. The POS interface needs significant changes—I'm removing the numeric keypad, updating the category pills to match the new grocery categories, simplifying the product cards, restructuring the right panel, changing the tax rate to 10%, and making the cash received field editable.

I also need to add the TICKET and REGISTRAR buttons, update the sidebar to show "Main Branch," and change the header to display the CAJA 04 - TERMINAL PRINCIPAL badge. Before rewriting the POS HTML, I should verify the server.js seed data to confirm it has the grocery products like milk, bread, coffee, and detergent already populated.
